The people of the district smelled a wondrous fragrance and heard celestial music that did not cease for an entire day.
Feng Min was a commoner of Shangyu in the Song dynasty. In his youth, he pursued hunting and sport. One day he encountered a giant serpent; seizing his spear, he intended to pierce it.

At that time, the snake was at the foot of a cliff, about to devour a yellow calf. Feng Min pushed down the rock upon it until it died. The snake had frequently caused calamities, yet Feng Min [remained unharmed].

Having practiced repentance and mindfulness of the Buddha for many years, he could not be harmed by snakes. One day, he invited his fellow practitioners of the Pure Land society to recite the *Amitābha Sūtra*;
with palms joined, he passed away.
Regarding the category of animals who attain rebirth,
the *Pusa chu tai jing* (Sutra on the Bodhisattva in the Womb) states: There was a dragon son who said to a garuḍa, "Since I have received this dragon body..."
He had never killed living beings nor disturbed the nature of sentient beings. After his life ended, he was destined to be reborn in the land of Amitābha Buddha.
During the Zhenyuan era of the Tang dynasty, a member of the Pei family from Hedong kept a parrot that constantly recited the Buddha’s name and did not eat after noon. When it approached its death...
With ten recitations, his breath ceased; he was cremated, and more than ten *śarīra* relics were obtained, brilliant and dazzling to the eye.
The monk Huiguan constructed a stupa using fired bricks to commemorate this marvel. Wei Gao, the Governor of Chengdu, composed an inscription for it, which includes the lines:
"Realizing the mark of emptiness within non-thought, leaving behind true bones after death."
Regarding the myna bird of Master Guan of Zheng’eng Temple in Huangyan, Song: he kept a myna bird that could speak and constantly recited the Buddha’s name without ceasing.

One day, it passed away while standing upright. He buried it in a hole in the earth, and shortly thereafter, a single purple lotus flower emerged from the tip of its tongue. — Recorded by Vinaya Master Lingzhi.

I once composed a eulogy for him, containing such lines as: "To stand and vanish, to be confined within a cage—these are but mundane matters; yet to transform into a purple lotus flower is truly marvelous.
Furthermore...
A man from Tanzhou kept a starling—locally known as a "baga'er. Seeing a monk reciting the Buddha’s name, it also learned to recite it.

He subsequently gave the bird to the monk. This monk constantly taught it to recite the name of Amitābha Buddha. Later, when the bird died, the monk buried it in a small coffin. A single lotus flower grew upon the grave mound.

Upon opening the coffin to look, he found that its roots had grown from the bird's own mouth. People composed a verse on the matter: The bird of the Western Land of Peace, Has come to this eastern world. Now that its life has ended, It returns to the Pure Land. Its roots emerge from its mouth; How wondrous! How marvelous! The power of the Buddha’s name Is truly inconceivable.
It is said: There was a bird known as a magpie that could recite the name of Amitābha along with the mouths of the monks.
When it died and was buried in level ground, lotus flowers sprouted. If people do not turn their hearts back [to the Dharma], what can be done?

For Amitābha Buddha has made this vow: "Any sentient being who recites my name shall surely be born in my land. Generally speaking, the term "sentient beings" includes those above, from devas and humans, down to...

Even minute creatures such as insects and ants can all be seen through this [practice]. If one observes in this way, this young magpie will surely be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss as a person of supreme goodness.
That humans do not know this, and that humans do not cultivate it—how truly lamentable!
The incident occurred outside the city walls of Tanzhou; for this reason, the city gate was named accordingly.
Lingquan, a monk of Puci Temple on the east side of Henghe Bridge in Hangzhou during the Daqing era, kept a dog. Whenever he encountered...
For many years, whenever the assembly of faithful from the Lotus Society gathered to recite sutras and chant the Buddha’s name, this dog would crouch down and listen quietly.
On the sixth day of the sixth month in the fifth year of the Kangxi era, according to the secular custom of bathing cats and dogs together, the dog was bathed in the pond.
Early the next morning, it died beside the latrine. The monks took pity on it and administered the Three Refuges for it while reciting dharanis.

When the dog was cremated and buried, it suddenly stood up, listened until the sounds of the Dharma were finished, and then lowered its front paws and prostrated itself as if in the gesture of *añjali*.

The entire assembly marveled at this. Since the dog manifested such a divine marvel, we know that while it crouched and lay low in its daily life, it must have directed its utmost sincerity and faith toward the Buddha.
Though its mouth could not speak, its mind silently recited; thus, it has attained rebirth in the Land of Peaceful Nurturing (*Sukhāvatī*) as one of supreme goodness.
Humans need have no doubt. If even a dog can manifest such a miraculous response, what then should be expected of those humans who practice the Pure Land with devotion?
Tian Yi composed this verse for it: In the vast, ancient garden, half is covered in *míwú* grass; Fortunately, the spirit-dog has not betrayed its purpose.
It treads upon the moss to welcome the virtuous guest, And barks at the moon through the vines to warn the stubborn man. Truly astonishing!
He himself revealed his true heart. Who would not investigate this public case? For many years he exhausted his sincerity;

when his conditions suddenly ended, his cremation was no different from the ordinary. Hai Shan Hu specially recorded this so that it might be passed down alongside the parrots and mynas, remaining undecaying.
Yet while those two birds were still able to speak it aloud, the dog merely held it in silence. This is truly a rare marvel throughout all antiquity.

Regarding the manifestation of the Buddha through mindfulness, Longshu said: "Although the Land of Ultimate Bliss is separated from here by a million worlds, in terms of its actual trace, it is not so far away.
However, because the Buddha’s nature of wisdom encompasses the void and all worlds, he is present everywhere."
Since all sentient beings, in every movement of thought and step, exist within the Buddha-nature, there is nothing that will not be efficacious when one’s sincerity is earnest and profound.
I have therefore carefully recorded those instances of response in the present life— drawn from the accounts in biographical collections and experienced through my own ears and eyes.
He requested the Buddha’s image from the Bodhisattva of Five Supernatural Powers at the Kukkutapāda Monastery in India, who traveled by means of his supernatural power to the Land of Utmost Bliss.

There he beheld Amitābha Buddha and presented this request: "The sentient beings of the Sahā world wish to be reborn in the Pure Land, yet they lack an image of the Buddha; I pray that you will deign to grant your permission."
The Buddha said, "You should go first; you shall soon manifest those five supernatural powers (pañcābhijñā).

Once you have returned to the holy deportment, you will reach a place where one Buddha and fifty bodhisattvas each sit upon lotus flowers atop tree leaves. Thereupon, [the image] was copied and circulated.

The title of this *Shenghui* (Assembly of Excellence) is by Chan Master Zongze of Changlu. Following the legacy of his distant ancestors, he established the Lotus Assembly of Excellence and universally exhorted others to practice Buddha-recitation.
One night, he dreamed of a man wearing a black cap and white robes, with a refined and beautiful countenance, who bowed and said, "I wish to enter your Lotus [Assembly]."

At the Huasheng Assembly, he requested that one name be written down. Zé asked what the name was; he replied, "Puhui. After it was written, he said again, "My elder brother Puxian also requests that his name be written together with yours.
Zé woke up and examined the "Detachment from the World" chapter (*Lokottara-parivarta*) of the *Avataṃsaka-sūtra*, where he found two bodhisattva names.
He then reflected: "The Sons of the Buddha who assist the Buddha in propagating the transformation must surely have sages and worthies who provide secret support for them. Thus, it was so.
Those who have gathered for this assembly must surely do so for no small reason; thus, these two bodhisattvas were appointed as the presiding leaders.
Regarding the most supreme Dharma-gate, Huiri of the Tang dynasty set sail across the sea, reached India, visited spiritual mentors, and inquired after the essential methods of the shortcut.
The scholars of India all praise the Pure Land. Upon reaching the country of Gandhāra, there was a statue of Avalokiteśvara on a great mountain to the northeast.
For seven days, [the practitioner] prostrated himself and fasted, vowing to end his life as his term of practice.

On the night of the seventh day, he suddenly beheld Avalokiteśvara, manifesting a body of purple-gold seated upon a precious lotus flower. The Bodhisattva extended his hand to stroke the practitioner’s head and said: "You wish to transmit..."
Regarding the Dharma of benefiting oneself and others, one should simply keep in mind Amitābha Buddha of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.

You should know that this single gateway of the Pure Land surpasses all other practices. Having spoken thus, he suddenly vanished. Returning to Chang’an, he universally exhorted others to practice mindfulness of the Buddha.

Regarding the couple who saw the Buddha, Ge Jizhi of Song was a native of Jurong and a descendant of Ge Zhi-chuan. He devoted himself to the study of the arts of the immortals throughout his life, while his wife, née Ji, alone maintained a spirit of singular sincerity in the recitation of the Buddha’s name.
In the thirteenth year of the Yuanjia era, while she was at her loom, she suddenly perceived a clarity and purity in the air; thereupon, she cast herself [down].
Zhu looked up toward the four quarters of the universe and saw a Buddha manifesting in the west, with precious canopies, banners, and streamers outshining the Milky Way.
He said joyfully, "The Sutra speaks of the Buddha of Infinite Life; could this be him? Facing the Buddha, he prostrated himself.
When Huiji arrived, struck by such a marvel, Ji pointed out the location of the Buddha to him. Huiji also saw half of the body, which soon vanished amidst auspicious clouds.
It was five-colored. All his kinsmen beheld it. From then on, many turned to the Buddha-dharma.

Once, there was a kingdom whose borders abutted those of the rākṣasas; although these rākṣasas devoured humans without restraint, the king made a pact with them from that time forward for the sake of the kingdom.

Within the community, each household was required to send one person in succession; no one was permitted to be killed unjustly. There was a family devoted to the Buddha who had only one son, and it was his turn to be sent.
His parents wailed in grief and exhorted him to recite the Buddha’s name with a sincere heart. By the power of the Buddha, the rākṣasa could not approach him.
When they went to look at him the next morning, they found the son still there; they took him back home. Thus ended the calamity of the rākṣasa.
This [possession] then subsided.
Chen Qi of Wangjiang, who had once falsely accused a person of murder, later saw a ghost appear before him; terrified, he hurriedly recited the name of Amitābha.

The Buddha—no ghost dared approach him. As he called upon the Buddha’s name unceasingly, the ghost finally vanished. Thereafter, he constantly practiced mindfulness of the Buddha and passed away peacefully while seated at the time of his death.
Half a year later, he manifested through the granddaughter of his own family, Myōkō, saying: "Because I called upon the name of Amitābha Buddha..."
Having already been reborn in the vessel-world of Ultimate Bliss, his movements and speech were exactly as they had been during his lifetime. Relatives and acquaintances all came to visit him.
After two or three days, his family members remarked, "It is a pity that while you were alive, you did not transmit the rites for the propitiation of the *xi-shen* (god of joy).
Qi then appeared with a countenance as solemn and dignified as in life, differing only in that his face bore a slight smile; this was because in the Western Land, one lives eternally.
He did not age; his head was like the spiral topknot (*śikhā*) of a Buddha, which is a gradual sign of attaining Buddhahood.
Nianfo Congbian, the Dhyāna Master Huisi of Mount Wuwei during the Sui dynasty, served the Buddha with a devoted mind. Consequently, he dreamed of Amitābha Buddha, who spoke to him.
The Dharma Master was naturally wise and surpassing others; his eloquence was unimpeded.

He recited the name of the Buddha to assist the deceased Zhang Jizu of Zhenjiang during the Song dynasty. Zhang was a devout believer in the Western Paradise, and when his wet nurse died, he frequently recited the name of Amitābha for her sake.

The Buddha. Posthumous offerings. One night, she dreamed that her mother came to thank her, saying: "I am indebted to you for your recitation of the Buddha's name; I have already been reborn in a good realm.

[In] Song Huaining County, Yingtian Village, there was a woman named Sister Niansan of the Ruan family who suffered from both eyes and was on the verge of blindness. She constantly recited "A... [the name of the Buddha].
Amitābha Buddha. She then attained enlightenment.
King Yama exhorted Lady Jiang of Zhulin Village in Jintan County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, who was about seventy years old; she died and was led to the underworld. Her life—
It was not yet finished. She was to be returned to Yama. The King asked, "Are you able to recite the sutras? She replied, "I am not.

The King said, "Since you cannot recite the sutras, you must instead recite the name of Amitābha Buddha. Once she was released and sent back, Lady Jiang said, "King Yama instructed me to practice mindfulness of the Buddha;
there is no longer any doubt about this. Therefore, she constantly practiced mindfulness of the Buddha until she reached nearly one hundred and twenty years of age before her death. Her...
Birth in the Pure Land can be taken as certain.
Liu Zhonghui of the Song dynasty, a native of Changxing in Huzhou, suffered from terrors in his dreams at night. Someone instructed him to practice the recitation of the Buddha’s name.
He then recited the name with utmost sincerity one hundred and eight times before retiring to bed. That night, his spirit and soul were serene.
From then on, he continued his recitation without ceasing;
by reciting the Buddha’s name, he was delivered from calamity.
Shao Biao, courtesy name Xiwen, of Jinjiang in the Song dynasty, while still a scholar, dreamed that he arrived at a government office where everyone was addressed as "Anfu" (Consul).
Delighted, Biao thought to himself, "Could this not mean that after I pass the examinations, I shall become an Anfu?

As he proceeded forward, he saw an official who asked him, "Do you know why you have not yet passed the examinations? Biao replied, "I do not know. The official then ordered someone to lead Biao away.
He saw a large cauldron boiling cicadas and shrimp. Upon seeing the tiger, they cried out the tiger’s name in human voices. The tiger then recited the name of Amitābha Buddha;
as soon as he had uttered it once, the cicadas and shrimp all transformed into yellow sparrows and flew away.

Later, the tiger indeed passed the imperial examinations and rose to the rank of Pacification Commissioner. From this, one sees that killing living beings obstructs one’s future prospects; therefore, one must not fail to exercise restraint. Furthermore, he saw...
The power of the Buddha is vast; one must not fail to revere it. Official rank has its own fixed destiny, and a person must not seek it through improper means.
Reciting the Buddha’s name can cease illness.
Wang Longshu of the Song dynasty boarded a boat and traveled to Zhenjiang. Because the lock was short of water, the vessel could not proceed.

He then borrowed the *Four Sutras*—which were the *Amitābha Sūtra* and others—from Mount Jinshan with the intention of collating them, carving woodblocks for printing, and disseminating them widely. Just as he raised his brush to begin the work—
His right hand was afflicted by wind; his fingers trembled of their own accord, making it difficult for him to write characters.

He then raised his finger and recited the name of Amitābha Buddha and Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva several times, offering prayers to be cured of this wind-illness so that he might successfully complete the transcription of this sutra.

After the prayer was finished, the finger no longer trembled; thus, it remained unharmed until the end of the volume. From this, one sees that the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are right before one’s eyes;
it is only that people’s faith does not reach its full measure. (Recorded by Longshu himself)
Regarding "Reciting the Buddha’s Name to Avoid Death":
There was an old woman who was blind in both eyes and had a young child lead her by the hand. She constantly recited the name of Amitābha Buddha.
One day, while resting beneath an old house, the house suddenly collapsed. The child ran away, but the old woman remained underneath. Then, there were two...
The wooden beams supported one another, protecting the old woman from above so that she was not crushed to death.
Li Ziqing of the Song dynasty suffered from chronic malaria that would not subside; the Layman of Longshu bestowed upon him a single method of instruction to be applied at the onset of the fever.

At that moment, he focused his mind exclusively on the recitation of the Buddha's name before taking the medicine. His son, being pure in faith, followed this practice; the symptoms were reduced by half that very day.
On the following day, he recited again, and was subsequently completely cured. From then on, he became steadfast in his faith and devoted himself to the recitation of the Buddha's name.

Sheli Bingxian was the Lady Gongren of the Middle Rank of Integrity (Lian Zhongdafu) during the Song dynasty. While she was embroidering a sixteen-foot image of Amitābha Buddha, when it had only reached half completion, śarīra suddenly appeared within the colored threads.
The entire household was filled with wonder and marvel.
Furthermore, the Lady Ren, wife of the Junior Master Zhongli of Zhenzhou, practiced the Way of the Western Paradise.

She carved an image of Amitābha Buddha four inches and eight fen in height, its niche adorned with great solemnity. She would often carry it upon her head while practicing the Way. Suddenly, from between the eyebrows of the image, [a light] burst forth.
The śarīra was as large as a grain of millet, its radiance illuminating those who beheld it.
It healed illnesses until they were cured.
A monk from Xiuzhou in the Song dynasty constantly recited the name of Amitābha Buddha and treated the illnesses of others; whenever anyone with an ailment requested his presence, he would go.
He was always able to recover completely. The people of the prefecture revered and believed in him as if he were a Buddha.
His descendants were spared from calamities.
In a village near Zhenjiang in the Song dynasty, there was an elderly man who, whenever there was something to attend to, would invariably join his palms at his forehead and recite "A... [Ānanda].

As for Maitreya Buddha: his grandson was only two or three years old when he followed his mother into the fields and suddenly went missing. The old man searched for him everywhere but could not find him.

Several days later, someone informed him that the boy was on the other side of a stream. When they went to look, they indeed found him there; footprints were seen leading all the way across the riverbank.
Since the stream was very deep, it was unknown by what means the child had crossed it. Furthermore, after a long time, [he] did not return.
Yang. People believed this was a response to his ancestor’s sincere recitation of the Buddha’s name. Regarding the liberation from shackles through the recitation of the Buddha’s name:
in the fifteenth year of the Zhizheng era, when Zhang Shicheng attacked Huzhou, the Chancellor of Jiangzhe fought him and captured four [prisoners].
Ten men were being sent to execution in a prison cart. That night they stayed at Niaoke Temple on West Lake.
It happened that Chan Master Dayou was strolling slowly along the corridor; the prisoners sought his help. The Master instructed them to recite with a sincere heart, "Namo Jiumu Jiunan Amituofo.
Three among them accepted his words and chanted without ceasing. At dawn they set out, and the prisoners' shackles were changed.

Shackles. When three prisoners arrived, there were insufficient instruments for their punishment; they could only be bound with ropes. Subsequently, upon interrogation, it was discovered that these were actually innocent civilians who had been abducted, whereupon they were released.
The Ghost Who Respected Mindfulness of the Buddha:
A man from Minghai Village had an old woman die who then attached herself to his family members and spoke at great length regarding her life’s affairs and the retributions of the underworld.
The villagers gathered around to listen. Among the crowd, there was one person who suddenly focused his mind on mindfulness of the Buddha.
The Buddha said to the old woman, "If you are always like this, why worry about not attaining the Way of Buddhahood?
She asked, "For what reason? He replied, "Because your mind contemplates Amitābha Buddha. She asked, "How do you know this? He replied, "Because I see that your body possesses radiance.

A village dweller who could not recognize a single character, by a mere fleeting thought, still caused the ghosts to show him respect; how much more so for those who have practiced for a long time? This is so.
Therefore, the merit of recollecting the Buddha is inconceivable.

The woman who transformed her female body into a male one was Wang Sanguan, the mother of the *zaolai* (guardian) of Mianshan, who served under the jurisdiction of the Qing Hangzhou Prefecture; she lived as a widow. At that age...
In his old age, he spent his days solely reciting the Buddha’s name. He donated all the ten-odd taels of gold he had accumulated to Lingyin Monastery.
In the fifth month of the first year of the Kangxi era, he fell ill and passed away. After half a day, he revived and said: "I am going to enter a male womb;
however, because the time for birth has not yet arrived, I have returned to tell you this. Now, please go find a midwife. Having spoken, he rested once more.
She passed away after half a meal.

Zhu Ruzhen of Tangxi Town, Qinghe County, was reborn in heaven through the power of reciting the Buddha’s name; her Dharma name was Jiyong. She was the daughter of Zhu Lang, an official of the Left Spring Palace.

She was the elder sister of Yi and served as my primary consort. Throughout her life, she was upright by nature and compassionate at heart. She placed deep faith in the Buddha-dharma and held the two great masters, Yulin and Jude, in the highest esteem and reverence.
From time to time, she also gave alms to monks and nuns; whenever she encountered those who were impoverished, suffering, or afflicted by illness, she would provide for them.
I shall certainly show them compassion and care. In the year of Xinchou, upon reaching my sixtieth birthday, I obtained Wang Longshu’s *Text on the Pure Land*.

My heart was filled with a fervent aspiration for it, and I consequently devoted myself exclusively to the practice of the Pure Land. Zhuo also followed this method, daily performing his recitations of the Buddha's name and chanting the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra* for five or six years.
Now, on the second day of the intercalary fourth month in the year of Kangxi Dingwei, at the hour of Chén...

[He] was carving [a statue]. Suddenly, he manifested a slight illness. On the third day of the month, at the hour of Xu (7–9 p.m.), he suddenly rose from his seated position, closed his eyes, and passed away in tranquility.

At the time of the encoffining, his countenance was as if alive; his joyful expression was still visible and could be admired. The assembly all marveled at this, knowing in advance that he would surely return to the auspicious realm.
On the night of the fifth seven-day period (the thirty-fifth day after death), he appeared in a dream to his daughter-in-law, Lady Chen, and said: "Previously, there was a heavenly..."
A deity appeared, holding a long-handled incense burner to welcome me; therefore, I departed immediately. He asked, "Are you aware that death has come?
I replied, "At first I was still dazed and did not know, but now I am aware. "I no longer take pleasure in wearing fine, colorful garments," he said.

He went straight into the inner chamber, opened the chest, and changed into a garment the color of green beans and a white silk robe, then departed with a serene air. I looked for him, but he was gone.
The daughter-in-law arose and related her dream in detail. I examined the boxes and found that indeed these two colored garments were there.
That same night, the old maidservant Guixiang also dreamed of the Lady seated with dignified composure upon a tiered platform in the front hall;
she wore a crown and was draped with strings of pearls, appearing like a celestial being. Since this same vision appeared once more, her rebirth in heaven is beyond doubt.
Thus it is. I have recorded this according to the facts, without a single word of falsehood, to inform the assembly. Believe this fully and wholeheartedly.

Practice the recitation of the Buddha's name early on and make the vow for rebirth in the Pure Land. At the moment of death, wondrous realms will naturally manifest before you; this shall certainly not fail. This is the clear evidence thereof.
Recorded specifically by the practitioner Baolian (Precious Lotus), to strengthen his own faith and to encourage all within the Dharma-realm to do the same.
Regarding "faith":
the Buddha has shown that if a person upholds the name of even a single Buddha, they shall obtain ten kinds of meritorious benefits in this present life.
First, throughout the day and night, they will constantly be protected by the great powerful divine generals of the heavens and their retinues, who remain hidden from sight. Second,
they will constantly be followed and protected by twenty-five great bodhisattvas, such as Avalokiteśvara and others, as well as all other bodhisattvas.
Third, they shall always be protected and remembered day and night by all Buddhas; Amitābha Buddha will constantly emit light to gather and sustain this person.
Fourth, no evil spirits—whether yakṣas or rākṣasas—nor any venomous snakes or poisonous dragons shall be able to harm them.
Poisons will be entirely unable to cause harm.
The five kinds of calamities involving fire, calamities involving water, enemies, bandits, swords, arrows, imprisonment, shackles, and the untimely or unjust deaths—
all these shall not befall them.
Sixth, all previously committed sins shall be completely extinguished; the lives of the victims they have killed shall attain liberation, and there shall be no further retribution.
Seventh, their dreams at night will be upright, or they may dream of the supreme and wondrous physical body of Amitābha Buddha.
Eighth, their minds are constantly joyful; their complexions are radiant and lustrous; their physical strength is full and flourishing; and all they do is auspicious and successful.
Ninth, they are always honored, supported, and prostrated to by all the people of the world, just as one would revere a Buddha.
Tenth, at the time of death, the mind is free from fear and right mindfulness manifests before them. They behold Amitābha Buddha and the assembly of holy Bodhisattvas,
who hold golden platforms in their hands to welcome and lead them to rebirth in the Western Pure Land,
where they shall enjoy supreme and wondrous bliss until the end of the future.

The Venerable Master Yuan of Mount Lu, a patriarch of successive generations, realized the profound purport of the Mahāprajñāpāramitā and was hailed as a Bodhisattva Protector of the Dharma in the East;

he practiced mindfulness of the Buddha during the six periods of the day and beheld sacred images on three occasions before being reborn in the Pure Land. The Great Master Zhiyi of Tiantai... [wondrous]...
Wuguang of the Fahua [School]: The founder of the teachings and contemplations of this single lineage, the patriarchal ancestor for ten thousand generations;

yet at birth he faced westward, resolving ten kinds of doubts, annotating the *Sutra of the Sixteen Contemplations*, and extensively discoursing on the Pure Land. Dashi Baizhang: The direct successor to the transmission of the Way from Mazu, venerated by all monastic communities throughout the land;
yet he prayed for sick monks and performed the funeral rites for deceased monks, ensuring they all returned to the Pure Land. Yong... [text truncated]
Chan Master Mingshou attained unimpeded eloquence and served as a pillar of the Chan school; he was particularly devoted to praising rebirth in the Western Pure Land in its highest grade.
Chan Master Sixin Xin of the Mingfu Monastery succeeded to the seat of Huanglong, where his dharma style flourished greatly;
yet he was deeply intent upon pure practice and authored the "Exhortation to Recite the Buddha’s Name," inspiring others to feel sorrow and give rise to faith. Chan Master Zhenxie Le...

The Master was a successor of Danxia Chun. This Dongshan lineage reached its greatest manifestation during his time. He established a hermitage at Putuo and devoted himself exclusively to the Western Paradise;
his *Jingtu ji* (Anthology on the Pure Land) remains in circulation today.

Chan Master Cishou Shen received the Dharma from Changlu Xin and focused his mind on the recitation of the Buddha’s name, asserting that no shortcut to cultivation surpasses the Pure Land. He established the Western Pathway.
In this assembly, Chan Master Yuanzhao Ben exhorted the multitude with bitter words; his lineage continued that of Tianyi, and he propagated the school of Xuedou.
His Dharma-thunder shook the earth, and as a model for two reigns, he concurrently cultivated the Pure Land practice, thereby securing his place in the Upper Grade.
Dharma Master Shizhi Xiao succeeded Master Xun of Yuetang; he thoroughly penetrated the scriptural divisions and transformed others through Pure Land practice, having once compiled the Great Canon.
Among various books, there is the *Wenlei of the Land of Bliss* (*Lepang Wenlei*), which has circulated in the world. Zen Master Yuantong Jichang studied Chan under National Teacher Mian Huaize;
he was devoted to the practice of the *nienfo samādhi*. He was moved by the descent of a golden-armored deity from heaven and by a dream in which a red lotus flower emerged from the earth.
From this, the Lotus School flourished throughout the Ten Continents. Zen Master Zhongfeng Hongyi received the Dharma [from him].
Master Gaofeng Miaohui was revered by his disciples like a mountain peak or a northern star; he said, "Chan is the Chan of Pure Land, and Pure Land is the Pure Land of Chan.
He composed one hundred poems on the aspiration for the Pure Land to exhort others to practice *nianfo*. Master Yudantan resided at the Shanfa Hall of Donglin Monastery on Mount Lu;
there he authored the *Lianzong baojian* (Jewel Mirror of the Lotus School), which was ordered by imperial decree to be carved into woodblocks and circulated for the sake of the Pure Land tradition.
During the Northern Song dynasty, Wang Yining, a Palace Attendant (Shizhi), styled himself a disciple of Amitābha.
Chao Yuezhi, a Hanlin Academician, replied in a letter to Zhao Ziaozhang, stating that the Western Pure Land is a teaching of true words and real words.

Chen Guan, a Palace Attendant, composed the "Record of the Pure Land Cloister at Yanqing Temple," in which he highly extolled the practice of *nianfo*. The above is a brief enumeration of several great venerable ones.
As for the other venerable masters who cultivated the Pure Land, they are beyond counting.
Master Lianchi said: "From our remote ancestors down to Youtan, there have been no successive generations of venerable masters who did not revere the Pure Land.
How can those of lower station among the scholar-officials fail to sever their doubts, resolve their wills, and advance with courageous vigor?"
The Complete Collection of Pure Land Scriptures, Volume Lower (End)
